✓ Environment & Climate.fact: Environment Protection Act, 1986. The Environment Protection Act 1986 is the umbrella legislation enacted after the Bhopal gas tragedy (1984), empowering the Centre to protect and improve the environment.

✓ Environment & Climate.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Environment & Climate.question: Which act deals with air pollution control in India?
✓ Environment & Climate.answer: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
✓ Environment & Climate.fact: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981. The Air Act 1981, passed after the 1972 Stockholm Conference, prevents and controls air pollution and is implemented through the CPCB.

✓ Environment & Climate.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Environment & Climate.question: Which act deals with water pollution control in India?
✓ Environment & Climate.answer: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
✓ Environment & Climate.fact: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974. The Water Act 1974 was India’s first pollution-control law and established the CPCB and state pollution control boards.

✓ Environment & Climate.question: Which act protects wildlife in India?
✓ Environment & Climate.fact: Wild Life Protection Act, 1972. The Wild Life Protection Act 1972 protects wild animals, birds and plants, and provides the legal basis for national parks and sanctuaries.

✓ Environment & Climate.question: Which act conserves forests in India?
✓ Environment & Climate.fact: Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980. The Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 restricts the diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes without central approval.

✓ Environment & Climate.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Environment & Climate.question: Which act deals with biodiversity in India?
✓ Environment & Climate.fact: Biological Diversity Act, 2002. The Biological Diversity Act 2002 implements the CBD and establishes the NBA, state boards and biodiversity management committees.

✓ Environment & Climate.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Environment & Climate.question: Which act deals with plastic waste management?
✓ Environment & Climate.fact: Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016. The Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016 regulate plastic waste generation, collection and recycling, and impose extended producer responsibility.

Næss's journal Inquiry was the first international journal to focus on this field.  The first US-based journal was Environmental Ethics, created in 1979. ✓ Food chain.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Food chain.question: Sea otters, a keystone species in _____ coastal regions, prey on sea urchins
✓ Food chain.fact: == Keystone species == A keystone species is a singular species within an ecosystem that others within the same ecosystem, or the entire ecosystem itself, rely upon.  Keystone species' are so vital for an ecosystem that without their presence, an ecosystem could transform or stop existing entirely.  One way keystone species impact an ecosystem is through their presence in an ecosystem's food web and, by extension, a food chain within said ecosystem.  Sea otters, a keystone species in Pacific coastal regions, prey on sea urchins.  Without the presence of sea otters, sea urchins practice destructive grazing on kelp populations which contributes to declines in coastal ecosystems within the northern pacific regions.  The presence of sea otters controls sea urchin populations and helps maintain kelp forests, which are vital for other species within the ecosystem.  == See also == Heterotroph Lithotroph Ecological pyramid Predator-prey interaction == References ==
